methodological_rigor.justification: Real-world retrospective analysis using Flatiron Health data. Two separate study designs: (1) utilization cohort (Jan 2023-June 2024) assessing abemaciclib prescribing in 3,170 eligible patients; (2) outcomes cohort (Jan 2011-June 2024) comparing IDFS/OS in 696 N+ high-risk vs 5,654 non-high-risk patients receiving ET only. Multivariable Cox models with adjustment for clinical covariates. Limitations: eligibility criteria highly restrictive (monarchE cohort 1 only), missing comorbidity/financial data, >50% missing Ki-67 may lead to misclassification.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Real-world cohort study documenting treatment gap (60% non-receipt of guideline-recommended abemaciclib) and associated risks of recurrence/death. LoE 2b: individual cohort study from EHR. Directly relevant to clinical practice: demonstrates 5-year IDFS 70.9% for N+ high-risk with ET alone (vs 83.6% abemaciclib in trial), similar to eTNBC (74.3%), supporting treatment intensification need.

reporting_quality.justification: Partial STROBE adherence with clear baseline characteristics, outcome definitions, and statistical methods. However, Flatiron data access restrictions limit replicability; missing comorbidities, functional status detail, and granular treatment information. Supplementary tables extensive but some referenced data not publicly available.

novelty_literature.justification: Identifies treatment gap in abemaciclib utilization post-FDA approval, with real-world outcomes demonstrating high recurrence risk. Extends prior single-institution studies (Rajendran, cited) to large multicenter cohort. Risk-by-nodal-status analysis novel contribution, though overall theme (underutilization of guideline-recommended therapy) incremental.

writing_presentation.justification: Clearly written with effective figures showing utilization barriers (age, nodal status) and outcome Kaplan-Meier curves. Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings and discusses safety tolerability. Some redundancy between results text and extensive supplementary data.

key_strengths: Large multicenter real-world cohort (n=3,170 utilization; n=6,365 outcomes) documenting 60% treatment gap in abemaciclib-eligible patients
Demonstrates 5-year recurrence/mortality risks equivalent to eTNBC when treated with ET alone, supporting guideline-directed therapy
Identifies demographic factors (age ≥65: 70.1% non-receipt) and nodal status barriers to treatment uptake
Stratified outcomes by nodal subgroups (N1/N1mi, N2, N3) with robust hazard ratios ≥1.6
key_concerns: Restrictive patient selection (monarchE cohort 1 criteria only) limits generalizability to broader N+ population
>50% missing Ki-67 may result in misclassification, potentially biasing non-high-risk group favorably
Missing data on comorbidities, patient preferences, and financial barriers—key drivers of non-utilization
Sensitivity analyses using initial diagnosis (not initiation of ET) provided in supplement but not emphasized
Outcomes comparison (HR >2.3 for recurrence) not adjusted for treatment received post-progression
chief_reviewer.rationale: Well-executed real-world outcomes study documenting treatment utilization gap and associated risks. Findings support guideline adherence and education initiatives. Suitable for Tier 2 publication with minor revisions addressing data limitations and discussion of intervention strategies.
